own_solution.law: RC charging: V_C(t) = E (1 - exp(-t/(R C))), tau = R C
assumptions: lamp circuit is a separate circuit

defect_reasons.missing_assumption: For the 60 ms break sentences (T7A5D, T3314) the answer relies on the capacitor not leaking, which the problem text does not state; this is a standard idealisation of an ideal capacitor and is listed in the authors' assumptions, so it does not make the item wrong.

notes: Checked all certified answers independently: base tau = 0.1 s, 12(1-e^-0.8) = 6.60805 V. Extra series R: 1.5 kOhm -> tau 0.13 s, x = 0.61538, 12(1-0.540433) = 5.5148 V; 3.5 kOhm -> tau 0.17 s, 4.50438 V; 7 kOhm -> tau 0.24 s, x = 1/3, 12(1-0.716531) = 3.40163 V. Break at 30 ms: 12(1-e^-0.3) = 3.11018 V; at 60 ms: 12(1-e^-0.6) = 5.41426 V. K values 250/400/750 ms all exceed 80 ms, answer unchanged. The regime predicate 'q > t' excludes the boundary q = t, at which the answer is also unchanged; no listed value reaches it, so this is immaterial. Minimal pairs hold: TB2B5/T0C95 share '3.5 kOhm resistor ... in series with the capacitor' and differ in 'earlier experiment' vs 'also ... this experiment'; TF284/TC6E4 share 3.5 kOhm in series and differ in attachment (lamp loop vs charging loop). TB645 and TF1CE are declared numeral-free twins of TB2B5 and TF284 rather than variants of the numbered sentences, which resolves my pass-1 observation about the missing numbers; no disagreement with my pass-1 strata or answers. T0C95's past tense ('was also connected ... in this experiment') is slightly awkward but unambiguous.
